method: Rechecked the lesson against OWASP SSRF Prevention, Python ipaddress, Linux pathname lookup, openat2(2), and Linux fs sysctl documentation. Corrected stale chapter/line references, clarified synthetic filesystem fixtures and capability-interface limits, and labeled illustrative snippets. Executed all five Python fences for syntax; ran the full filesystem fixture and the offline URL-policy fixture under Python 3.10.9. The URL fixture's complete 20-case stdout matched the published text block byte-for-byte; the preserved ERR-137 verifier passed 10/10 and the W6 verifier passed 5/5. No provider calls, DNS requests, or HTTP requests were made. Production build generated 403 pages; Pagefind indexed 403 pages / 15,456 words. Light/dark full-page screenshots were visually checked at 1300px viewport: article width 792px, document scrollWidth 1300px, one rendered Mermaid SVG; each image is 1300x14982. The only initial browser console error was the existing /favicon.ico 404.
limitations: The filesystem example verifies fixed local fixtures; it does not exercise concurrent path replacement, hard-link abuse, production directory permissions, or an OS sandbox.
The URL example is a fixed policy fixture. It makes no DNS or HTTP calls and does not validate a real HTTP transport, DNS pinning, redirect handling, proxy, firewall, or deployed egress rules.
The capability-oriented interface is illustrative and not independently run; it does not demonstrate production identity binding, ID lifecycle, revocation, or an operating-system capability boundary.
The historical 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 provider/network observations remain limited to their recorded endpoint and lack complete raw traces for independent historical replay.
